Eve - Album 1: WHO

Our Deepest Condolences

"Our deepest condolences"

[Intro]

Home again Different somehow Same old streets But quieter now

Suitcase waiting Keys in my hand Trying to understand What grief demands

[Verse 1]

I came back home to organize goodbye Call the chapel, choose the flowers, try To answer questions I was never ready for Names and dates and papers by the door

Grandma always made things seem so light Even when the world refused to turn out right Now every room feels larger than before And every little sound comes through the floor

I make some coffee Forget to drink Sign another page Try not to think

There are arrangements There are calls There are photographs Still on the walls

[Pre-Chorus]

Everyone says Take all the time you need

But time keeps asking What comes next of me

[Chorus]

Our deepest condolences Soft words everyone knows They land so gently Then disappear where sorrow goes

Our deepest condolences I’m grateful, I suppose But nothing anyone can say Can make this house feel whole

So I nod And I breathe And I thank them when they leave

Our deepest condolences

And another door will close

[Verse 2]

The family lawyer comes around at noon Dark suit, careful voice, leaving soon He carries folders, papers tied and neat And places one old key beside my seat

Apparently Grandma left me more than home An estate somewhere I never knew she’d owned A massive house outside the edge of town Hidden past a road that winds around

And books

A collection

Already moved inside

Boxes upon boxes Waiting where they hide

He gives directions Tells me when to go Says everything is mine now

Which is strange enough to know

[Pre-Chorus]

I thought I knew her Every habit, every room

Now she’s left me A secret bigger than the truth

[Chorus]

Our deepest condolences And keys I never knew A house she never mentioned And a library waiting too

Our deepest condolences Wrapped in legal prose Every answer that I came here for Has somehow grown

So I nod And I breathe And I take what she left me

Our deepest condolences

And one more mystery

[Verse 3]

Gray sky hanging over cemetery stone I thought I’d have to say goodbye alone But figures gather slowly through the rain People I have never seen or heard her name

Eleven standing quietly nearby Dark clothes, covered faces, lowered eyes Not family Not neighbors No one I recognize

Yet every one of them Seems to know exactly why

One by one they come One by one they stand Voices low and heavy Cold against my hands

Our deepest condolences

The same words every time

I thank them all for coming Though none of them are mine

[Bridge]

Who were you, Grandma? Who did you know? What kind of life Did you never show?

Eleven strangers Eleven hidden faces Eleven shadows Standing in familiar places

Maybe grief makes everything strange Maybe I’m searching because something changed

Maybe tomorrow I’ll understand

Maybe that house Will tell me what I can’t

[Final Chorus]

Our deepest condolences The rain begins to fall Eleven figures disappear Beyond the cemetery wall

Our deepest condolences I whisper one goodbye Lay my hand against the stone And let myself finally cry

You were my home You raised me right You kept me standing Every night

And whatever you left waiting Whatever I may find

Tomorrow I’ll go see it

Tomorrow I’ll step inside

[Outro]

One key One address One estate I never knew

A library waiting With books she never showed me

I look back once At Grandma’s name

Then start walking home

Tomorrow

I’ll find out what she left behind
